name: Rear Five-Link Suspension Links
description: The Gen 6 rear is a 5-link independent: per side a lower control arm (spring link, also carries the shock), an upper control arm (upper lateral/camber link), an upper trailing arm, a lower trailing arm (traction link) and a toe link (GM 'adjust link'). GM uses stamped steel links with lightening holes. Camber is adjusted with an eccentric cam bolt at the LCA inner pivot and toe with an eccentric at the toe-link inner pivot. Nearly every rear link fastener is torque-to-yield (torque + angle) per GM.

components.name: Rear lower control arm (spring link)
components.description: Stamped steel lateral link from the cradle to the bottom of the knuckle. It holds the coil spring in a pocket and the lower shock mount, so it carries most of the vertical load. The inner pivot uses an M14 eccentric cam bolt for camber adjustment. An aero cover with push-pin fasteners covers the arm. Race options: tubular arms (coilover-only versions exist) and spherical inner bearings.
components.location: Inner pivot approx (x 2.90, y 0.24, z +/-0.30) to knuckle approx (x 2.84, y 0.18, z +/-0.70); spring pocket approx (x 2.88, y 0.23, z +/-0.50).

hardware.item: Rear lower control arm inner bolt (M14 cam bolt) + cam washer + nut
hardware.spec: M14 eccentric cam bolt, cam washer, nut (18/21 mm)
hardware.partNumber: Per BMR-published GM list: bolt 11609598, washer 11611695, nut 11516382 (verify - SG3 kit 84408106 supplies new cam bolt/washer/nut)
hardware.torqueSequence: Set camber at alignment with car at ride height, then 115 N·m + 90-105 deg (GM SG3). Some GM SI years list +75-90 deg - verify for your model year.
hardware.reuse: Replace (TTY) - GM: discard bolt, nut and cam washer

hardware.item: Rear lower control arm outer bolt + nut (to knuckle)
hardware.spec: Flange bolt + nut, 18 mm / 15 mm wrench per BMR
hardware.notes: First-pass value from GM SI listing (TightTorque); angle from BMR LCA361. [2026-10 check] BMR LCA361 gives 111 ft-lb + 90–105° (LCA to spindle), and TightTorque (GM 2016–18 SI) gives 150 N·m first pass, so the two agree. Not found in a GM primary document; stays typical.

hardware.item: Lower control arm cover push-pin retainers
hardware.notes: Cover often deleted on race cars.

installNotes: Mark cam bolt position before removal to retain alignment (BMR).
Support LCA with a jack while removing; lower slowly - spring is under load.
Install loosely, install spring and shock, raise to ride height, then align and final-torque the inner cam bolt.
inspection: Check spring pocket for cracks, cam bolt witness marks, and arm for bends.

components.description: Stamped steel lateral link at the top of the knuckle. Together with the LCA it sets camber and camber gain. Fixed length from the factory; adjustable race arms allow equal camber side-to-side and more negative camber without relying on the slipping OE eccentric.

components.name: Rear toe link (GM 'adjust link')
components.description: Lateral link that controls rear toe. The inner end on the cradle uses an M12 eccentric cam bolt for toe adjustment; the outer end bolts to the knuckle. Its height relative to the other links determines rear bump steer. Rod-end race toe links with lockout washers eliminate eccentric slip and allow precise toe/bump-steer setting.
components.location: Inner approx (x 3.00, y 0.27, z +/-0.32) to knuckle approx (x 3.00, y 0.26, z +/-0.68) (behind axle line - verify).

components.name: Rear camber and toe eccentric cam bolts / lockouts
components.description: Eccentric cam bolt + cam washer sets at the LCA inner pivot (camber) and toe-link inner pivot (toe). The OE eccentrics give roughly 1 deg of range and tend to slip under high cornering loads, so race cars lock them out with slotted plates/washers or replace them with adjustable links.
